display.title: Bubby's Stories and Zaidy's Songs
display.summary_short: A grandmother tells her grandchildren five classic Jewish stories in English, and the grandfather sings Shabbos and Yom Tov songs, closing with a blessing.
display.summary_long: A home recording made by a grandmother and grandfather for their grandchildren. The grandmother tells five stories. As a young school helper, the Baal Shem Tov remembers his father's words, 'Fear nothing but Hashem', and drives off a man in a bear skin who frightened children on their way to shul on Friday night. Yosef, who always bought the best for Shabbos, buys a huge fish and finds a wicked man's lost diamond inside. Rabbi Yitzchak, a poor and childless man, finds a precious diamond but will not let it decorate an idol; he drops it into the sea, and an angel promises him a son, Rashi. Rabbi Meir refuses to travel on Shabbos and is left alone in the desert, where a lion guards him and carries him back to the caravan. A boy playing 'judge' shows how to prove that a Jewish shopkeeper did not steal a butcher's money, saving the whole town. The grandfather then sings Shabbos zemiros and Yom Tov songs, and the grandparents close with a blessing in English and Yiddish.
display.lesson: Fear only Hashem, honor Shabbos, and Hashem protects those who are honest and faithful to His mitzvos.

advisories.note: The young Baal Shem Tov beats a man disguised as a bear; a lion approaches a rabbi alone in the desert.
A Jewish shopkeeper is falsely accused and jailed, and the townspeople talk of expelling the Jews.

privacy.note: Home recording by grandparents for their grandchildren.
A grandchild is called by name while the stories are told.
